reason: The design's headline advantage ('passes every drive gate at mu 0.15 on BOTH stages ... the first desmo-family drive that does', row verdict) rests on a gate the screener re-read for this design. Stage 1 is read on the built blended groove: the cap (back-drive) side is gated only outside the blend, and the blend is BLEND_PLACEHOLDER. Under the family's linear reading, the same claim placement has the cap side at 35.05 deg at K 0 against the mu 0.15 gate of 34.47 and fails at K 0 (fast 86.52); it passes at mu 0.135 (gate 35.31, fast 13.31), so its linear-read friction limit is mu ~0.139 (tan(43 - 35.05)), the same as desmo-slipper's measured jam at mu 0.14. The score does not move: fast 13.31 at mu 0.087 or 0.135 on the linear read equals the claim (docs/alignment/remeasure/desmo-conecut-knuckle-3r_s1read_check.json; docs/concepts/verify/desmo-conecut-knuckle-3r_v_probe_fast.json). The genuine gain is stage 2: the inverted slot keeps its PA stroke 64.5 deg of K up to mu 0.15 (61.0 at 0.20). Not gamed: no number ranks the design above a better one; the friction claim is a label.
